capabilities: Cached original Module forwards read packed offset-zero input directly and write the last stage into a fresh owning GPU output.
Optional view packing, checked NN execution and frozen owning error flags use one queue submission, with no full-sized input/output bridge copies for contiguous offset-zero input.
Rust graph.forward_tensor, Python graph.forward_tensor and WASM graph.forwardTensor expose the same backend; old explicit dispatch/snapshot semantics interoperate.

New native tests cover 8 graph patterns, 5 input layouts and 6 dense kernel/accumulation combinations, invalid values, rejection atomicity, singleton/rectangular boundaries and immutable output lifetime.
boundaries: Fresh output buffers, boundary bindings, small stage flag copies and a separate guard compute pass remain. Shape views may require packing. Not allocation-free or all-operations fusion.
O(parameter values) host comparison remains on original Module calls; no implicit migration of host-backed pure Tensor, generic autograd or ModuleTrainer.
One compute pass for existing graph nodes plus a guard pass; no GPU timestamp claim. All stage math and tolerances unchanged.
Same-page browser baseline/candidate runs use separate WASM modules/devices. Exact browser physical GPU and host exclusivity UNKNOWN.
Native versions run serially in separate processes, each with rotated eager PyTorch controls. Differences do not isolate a single phase or prove fastest-PyTorch throughput.
Burst means eight independent fixed-input forwards with a final completed host observation, not recurrent decoding.

Single-call d2h timings do not uniformly improve. Browser samples are visibly quantized. A cross-process Torch control shifts substantially at seed 17/small shape; all raw/control timings remain retained, not attributed entirely to the code change.
No CUDA/Furnace, push, merge, or release in this slice. Preliminary dirty-source logs are retained only as preflight, not admitted timing evidence.
